name: Zebra BI
subcategory: IBCS reporting visuals for Power BI and Excel
tagline: Custom visuals for Power BI and Excel that render IBCS-style variance charts, small multiples and waterfalls without manual chart surgery.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The actual chart grammar here is not secret: actual vs plan vs previous year, absolute and relative variance columns, consistent scaling across a grid of small multiples, waterfalls that respect sign. An agent can build a convincing IBCS-ish charting layer over your own CSV in a weekend, and for personal analysis that is genuinely enough. What you cannot one-shot is the part that matters to the people who pay: it lives inside Power BI and Excel, next to slicers, cross-filtering, drill-through and a formatting pane, in a report someone else opens on Monday. Writing a real Power BI custom visual with the visuals SDK is possible but it is a project, not a session, and matching the tooltip, print and cross-highlight behavior is where the weeks go. Build it as a local dashboard if you own your data; do not expect to drop it into a corporate report.
coreLoopDIY: Loads a CSV of actual/plan/previous-year by period and category and renders IBCS-style variance charts, variance columns and a consistently scaled small multiples grid you can export.
requirements: a CSV export of your data with actual, plan and prior-year columns
willingness to leave Power BI and look at your numbers in a browser instead
whatYouLose: Lives inside Power BI and Excel: slicers, cross-filtering, drill-through, the formatting pane, report sharing
Dynamic comments pinned to data points that survive refresh
Hundreds of edge cases in scaling, sign handling, label collision and small-number formatting
Print and PowerPoint export that looks like someone proofread it
Anything resembling IBCS conformance you can point at in a review
moatNotes: The moat is being a first-class citizen of someone else's report canvas. Charting is the easy half.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is a controller or FP&A lead who already lives in Power BI and Excel, and the alternative is an analyst hand-building variance charts every month and getting the scaling wrong. Zebra BI sells consistency and time back inside tools the company already standardized on, plus a standards story that ends arguments in review meetings. A local dashboard you built yourself does not help when the CFO opens the shared report. If you are the only consumer of your own numbers, none of that applies.
notes: The charts are learnable in an afternoon; being embeddable in the tool your finance team already uses is not.
prompt:
Build a local IBCS-style variance reporting dashboard. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + TypeScript + React + D3 (d3-scale, d3-shape, d3-array only, hand-rolled SVG, no chart library). Plain CSS, no UI kit. Everything runs with `npm install && npm run dev`.

Data input: a file picker and drag-and-drop for a CSV with columns: period, category, actual, plan, prior. Parse with d3-dsv. Ship a sample.csv with 12 monthly periods and 6 categories so the app is useful on first run. Keep parsed data in memory only, no persistence beyond a localStorage cache of the last file.

Render these chart primitives as reusable React components, all monochrome with variance in red/green and hatched fills for plan:
1. Time series column chart: actual columns, plan as thin overlaid reference bars, prior year as a line.
2. Variance columns: absolute variance (actual minus plan) as bars above/below zero, plus a second stacked panel for relative variance in percent with a plus/minus label.
3. Category comparison: horizontal bars sorted descending with integrated variance bars to the right.
4. Waterfall: category contributions bridging from plan total to actual total, correct sign handling, subtotal column.
5. Small multiples grid: one time series per category, all panels sharing one common y-scale computed across the whole dataset, panel titles and a single shared axis.

Hard requirements: one global scaling mode toggle (shared scale vs per-panel), number formatting with thousands separators and a configurable unit divisor, no chart junk (no gridlines, no 3D, no legends where direct labels work), labels suppressed when they would collide, tooltips on hover showing actual/plan/prior/variance.

Also: a period range filter, a category multi-select, and per-chart export to SVG and PNG via canvas. Add a print stylesheet that lays the charts out on A4 landscape.

Out of scope, do not attempt: Power BI custom visual packaging, Excel add-in, cross-filtering across charts, drill-through, data comments, live database connectors, auth.

Write a README that states plainly what this is not: it is a local viewer for your own CSV, not a report you can share inside Power BI.
